The list of hidden modules below it is derived from MODULE_GROUPS, i.e. the ROWS. When the two disagree the page reports a number it cannot show you: three flags (`xero_integration`, `jodie_ai`, `rto_extension`) existed only in LAUNCH_FLAGS, and two of those three were the ONLY flags defaulting to false — so the page said '2 hidden' and listed nothing". Those three now have rows: rto_extension at :121, xero_integration at :165, jodie_ai at :233 (and useFeatureFlags.ts:73-77 confirms jodie_ai and rto_extension are the two false-by-default flags that produced the operator's "2 hidden"). operator_audit.operator_verbatim: "Schema builder makes no sense. I have no idea how to use it… 'Fit' icon does nothing."
operator_audit.evidence: The Schema Builder canvas renders at ZERO HEIGHT in the version production consumes, so nothing on it — including the Fit icon — can work. The estate's own commit cd9c901e (2026-08-26, one day before this audit) records the measurement: "Measured on suite.crm7.app today: .react-flow 1136x0, 44 nodes in the DOM, 16 inside the window, toolbar reporting '44 entities', canvas blank", and explains why the earlier fix was inert (@xyflow/react v12 spreads its own wrapperStyle AFTER the caller's `style`, so the position/height passed through that prop are always overwritten). That commit is part of @bsuite/schema-builder 1.6.1. MEASURED: `npm view @bsuite/schema-builder versions` → latest published is **1.6.0**; 1.6.1 was never published. crm7 origin/main pins `"@bsuite/schema-builder": "^1.6.0"` with pnpm-lock resolving `version: 1.6.0`, and BSU pins the same; conduit is still on 1.5.1. So the fix exists only in the monorepo working tree and reaches zero apps. On the 'Fit' sub-ask specifically: a handler does exist (packages/schema-builder/src/components/SchemaCanvas.tsx:647-652, `fitView({duration:400, padding:0.2, maxZoom:1.2})` against `minZoom={0.05}` at :909) and is present in the installed dist, but a fitView against a 1136x0 container cannot produce a visible result. operator_audit.operator_verbatim: "Says 2 hidden modules but no modules that show they are not visible"
operator_audit.evidence: The three orphaned flags now have rows and working toggles, and a build-failing invariant stops the defect recurring. ROOT CAUSE AND FIX, recorded in the file: crm7/src/pages/settings/module-visibility.tsx:33-52 — "the 'Hidden Modules' stat counts ... the FLAGS. The list of hidden modules below it is derived from MODULE_GROUPS, i.e. the ROWS. When the two disagree the page reports a number it cannot show you: three flags (`xero_integration`, `jodie_ai`, `rto_extension`) existed only in LAUNCH_FLAGS, and two of those three were the ONLY flags defaulting to false — so the page said '2 hidden' and listed nothing". Those three now have rows: rto_extension at :121, xero_integration at :165, jodie_ai at :233 (and useFeatureFlags.ts:73-77 confirms jodie_ai and rto_extension are the two false-by-default flags that produced the operator's "2 hidden"). TOGGLES ARE REAL, NOT COSMETIC: `<Switch ... onCheckedChange={(checked) => handleToggle(item.key, checked)} />` at :527-529, and `saveMutation` at :297-325 writes `feature_flags` back to tenant settings (`.update({ feature_flags: ... })` at 314-315), reading back from the same column at :261,275. REGRESSION GUARD: src/pages/settings/module-visibility.test.tsx:84-97 asserts every `LAUNCH_FLAGS` key has a MODULE_GROUPS row, 101-109 asserts the converse, 115 rejects duplicates. crm7 issue #1682 ("/settings/module-visibility lists hidden modules but has no working control to enable them") is CLOSED and the code backs it.

operator_audit.operator_verbatim: "Schema builder makes no sense. I have no idea how to use it… 'Fit' icon does nothing."
operator_audit.evidence: The Schema Builder canvas renders at ZERO HEIGHT in the version production consumes, so nothing on it — including the Fit icon — can work. The estate's own commit cd9c901e (2026-08-26, one day before this audit) records the measurement: "Measured on suite.crm7.app today: .react-flow 1136x0, 44 nodes in the DOM, 16 inside the window, toolbar reporting '44 entities', canvas blank", and explains why the earlier fix was inert (@xyflow/react v12 spreads its own wrapperStyle AFTER the caller's `style`, so the position/height passed through that prop are always overwritten). That commit is part of @bsuite/schema-builder 1.6.1. MEASURED: `npm view @bsuite/schema-builder versions` → latest published is **1.6.0**; 1.6.1 was never published. crm7 origin/main pins `"@bsuite/schema-builder": "^1.6.0"` with pnpm-lock resolving `version: 1.6.0`, and BSU pins the same; conduit is still on 1.5.1. So the fix exists only in the monorepo working tree and reaches zero apps. On the 'Fit' sub-ask specifically: a handler does exist (packages/schema-builder/src/components/SchemaCanvas.tsx:647-652, `fitView({duration:400, padding:0.2, maxZoom:1.2})` against `minZoom={0.05}` at :909) and is present in the installed dist, but a fitView against a 1136x0 container cannot produce a visible result. The broader ask ("makes no sense, I have no idea how to use it") has no shipped evidence at all — no onboarding, no guided first-run; the quick-start tip work is 1.4.0 and predates the zero-height regression.

compliance_risk.detail: R80.4's `applyPlacementFunding` implements funding as an ADDITIVE deduction on a rate that already had quote funding netted out, guarded by an `inheritedProgramIds` exclusion list that is always empty. The operator's model is REPLACEMENT: the placement's second look refines a broad category estimate into an individual-specific amount, it is not a second set of funding. So the module implements the wrong model, not merely a broken guard — writing `fundingProgramIds` would not make it correct.
compliance_risk.code_evidence: R80.4 src/awards/calculate.ts nets funding at quote time (`funded: quoted - fundingPH`); src/awards/quotes.ts applyPlacementFunding subtracts again (`placement.hourly - additionalPerHour`). The whole FundingProgram path is unwired — zero call sites in the shipped UI, which prices via FundingScheme.
compliance_risk.why_not_in_production: The live calculator never calls applyPlacementFunding. In crm7 — where placements and invoicing actually live — funding is a SEPARATE LEDGER: funding_claims/funding_milestones claim from the funding body and never touch placements.charge_rate. The placement rate is overwritten wholesale from the approved quote (charge_rate_quotes_propagate_approval), and billingEngine prices the wages line straight off it. The one mechanism that did net funding against a charge rate, `funding_offsets`, was deliberately retired by supabase/migrations/20260830010000_retire_funding_offsets_scheme_model.sql under the standing ruling that "R80.4's funding calculation is the only acceptable method of calculation".
compliance_risk.recommended_action: Re-spec to replacement semantics, or delete the module — crm7 already owns the second look and already keeps it off the charge rate. Do NOT fix by writing fundingProgramIds.

notes: Refuses to save a quote with any unpriced line.

earlier_pass.detail: The placement funding anti-double-count guard does not hold: the field the placement reads for 'already priced into the quote' funding (quote.meta.fundingProgramIds) is declared and read but never written anywhere, so it resolves to [] and a program already priced into a quote can be re-elected and subtracted a second time at placement.
earlier_pass.code_evidence: src/awards/quotes.ts: `QuoteMeta.fundingProgramIds` is declared, and convertToPlacement() reads `inheritedProgramIds: quote.meta?.fundingProgramIds ?? []`. A repo-wide search for any assignment to `fundingProgramIds` (github search_code, query `fundingProgramIds`) returns only the declaration and this one read site — no call site anywhere in the repo sets it on a quote's meta when building/issuing a quote, so it is always `[]` and applyPlacementFunding()'s inherited-vs-additional split can never actually exclude a quote-scope program from being re-counted at placement.
earlier_pass.caveat: Owner reports the calculator prices correctly in the cases he has tested. This is a specific unguarded path, not a general correctness claim. Production was 13 PRs behind development as of 20 Aug — verify on the deployed host before acting.

entry_point: automatic on Save, when signed in
sibling_enumeration_method: sibling_class assigned in pass 1 from the reusable pattern the surface is built from, normalised in pass 3; count is the number of index rows sharing that class

compliance_risk.detail: R80.4's `applyPlacementFunding` implements funding as an ADDITIVE deduction on a rate that already had quote funding netted out, guarded by an `inheritedProgramIds` exclusion list that is always empty. The operator's model is REPLACEMENT: the placement's second look refines a broad category estimate into an individual-specific amount, it is not a second set of funding. So the module implements the wrong model, not merely a broken guard — writing `fundingProgramIds` would not make it correct.
compliance_risk.code_evidence: R80.4 src/awards/calculate.ts nets funding at quote time (`funded: quoted - fundingPH`); src/awards/quotes.ts applyPlacementFunding subtracts again (`placement.hourly - additionalPerHour`). The whole FundingProgram path is unwired — zero call sites in the shipped UI, which prices via FundingScheme.
compliance_risk.why_not_in_production: The live calculator never calls applyPlacementFunding. In crm7 — where placements and invoicing actually live — funding is a SEPARATE LEDGER: funding_claims/funding_milestones claim from the funding body and never touch placements.charge_rate. The placement rate is overwritten wholesale from the approved quote (charge_rate_quotes_propagate_approval), and billingEngine prices the wages line straight off it. The one mechanism that did net funding against a charge rate, `funding_offsets`, was deliberately retired by supabase/migrations/20260830010000_retire_funding_offsets_scheme_model.sql under the standing ruling that "R80.4's funding calculation is the only acceptable method of calculation".
compliance_risk.recommended_action: Re-spec to replacement semantics, or delete the module — crm7 already owns the second look and already keeps it off the charge rate. Do NOT fix by writing fundingProgramIds.

notes: Signed-out users still save to this browser only; the panel states which state applies via quoteMirrorStatus().

earlier_pass.detail: The placement funding anti-double-count guard does not hold: the field the placement reads for 'already priced into the quote' funding (quote.meta.fundingProgramIds) is declared and read but never written anywhere, so it resolves to [] and a program already priced into a quote can be re-elected and subtracted a second time at placement.
earlier_pass.code_evidence: src/awards/quotes.ts: `QuoteMeta.fundingProgramIds` is declared, and convertToPlacement() reads `inheritedProgramIds: quote.meta?.fundingProgramIds ?? []`. A repo-wide search for any assignment to `fundingProgramIds` (github search_code, query `fundingProgramIds`) returns only the declaration and this one read site — no call site anywhere in the repo sets it on a quote's meta when building/issuing a quote, so it is always `[]` and applyPlacementFunding()'s inherited-vs-additional split can never actually exclude a quote-scope program from being re-counted at placement.
earlier_pass.caveat: Owner reports the calculator prices correctly in the cases he has tested. This is a specific unguarded path, not a general correctness claim. Production was 13 PRs behind development as of 20 Aug — verify on the deployed host before acting.

operator_audit.operator_verbatim: "We did recently have the ability to add new elements on page but this is now missing again."
operator_audit.evidence: The affordance IS restored and is wired to real rendering, but what you add does not survive a reload. Restored path: header button at crm7/src/components/layout/CRM7Header.tsx:317-332 (renders when `canEditPages`, becomes the 'Add element' trigger while the editor is open) → PageEditorLauncher.tsx:542-565 opens WidgetPalette and dispatches `crm7-add-entity-widget` → @bsuite/page-builder PageGridLayout's listener (dist/PageGridLayout.js:481-510) calls `addWidget()` and `onRegisterEntityWidget()` → crm7's adapter renders the real component (pageGridLayoutAdapter.tsx:270-295 for `builtin:` widgets, :296-320 for entity tables). /dashboard is covered: Dashboard.tsx:130-134 imports PageGridLayout from the crm7 ADAPTER, and the adapter injects `createEntityWidget`/`onRegisterEntityWidget` at pageGridLayoutAdapter.tsx:456-457 — without that injection the package's listener would never register (`if (!createEntityWidget ...) return`, dist:482). There is also an in-canvas '+ Add card' at InPlaceCardEditing.tsx:594. MEASURED: `npx vitest run src/components/platform/PageEditorLauncher.builtin-widgets.test.tsx src/components/platform/PageEditorLauncher.test.tsx` → 2 files, 12 tests passed. THE GAP: the added widget is not durable. The layout item IS persisted (usePageGridLayout.js:608-620 `addWidget` → `commitItems` → `setSavedLayout`), but its identity is not: crm7's widget registry is a module-scoped in-memory Map (src/lib/page-builder/widgetRegistry.tsx:31 `const registry = new Map()`
